why: LANDED 2026-10-27 (phase-515 R4): `Node::create_timer_oneshot(period, callback)`, rclrs 0.7.0's verb, on this node's default `SchedContext`; it fires once, `period` after creation, then goes inert; `Executor::reset_timer` re-arms it for one more shot. `period` takes a `TimerDuration` or a `core::time::Duration` (the `std::time::Duration` an rclrs caller passes). ENVELOPE (stated on the method): it returns the timer's `HandleId`, not an rclrs `Timer` object, because the timer lives in the executor's static table -- `Executor::cancel_timer` / `reset_timer` take the id; there is no `IntoTimerOptions` (a clock choice is `create_timer_on_clock`). Test: `node_creates_rclrs_repeating_oneshot_and_inert_timers`. PRIOR ROW: **rclrs 0.7.0 CONVERGED ON OUR SHAPE.** 0.5.1 had one `create_timer`; 0.7.0 has `create_timer_inert` / `create_timer_oneshot` / `create_timer_repeating` -- the same three modes our `TimerMode` carries, arrived at independently. Ours are a mode SET ON an entity in the static table (`set_inert`, `set_oneshot`, `set_repeating`) because a static table cannot grow a timer at runtime and re-arming is how a one-shot is reused; rclrs constructs one per mode. Same model, different placement -- so this is no longer the divergence the 0.5.1 comparison recorded, and W5 should consider matching the verb.
